methodology_note: Bank: residual income (cash earnings less one-offs, less a cost-of-equity charge on opening tangible book) discounted at the AUD cost of equity, plus opening tangible book, plus a Gordon terminal on Y5 residual income. Deposits are operating funding, so net debt is zero and no owner-FCF DCF is built. Same family as ANZ.AX (residual income on TBV), SRBK and SOFI.

valuation_philosophy.methodology: Residual income on tangible book value, discounted at cost of equity -- a bank model, NOT an owner-FCF DCF
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Bendigo and Adelaide Bank is an APRA-regulated authorised deposit-taking institution. Its operating cash flow (+A$6.1bn FY21, -A$3.3bn FY22, +A$5.7bn FY23, -A$0.3bn H1 FY26) is loan and deposit flow, not owner earnings; deposits (A$86.0bn) and the A$10.4bn of debt issuance and loan capital are the raw material of net interest income, not net debt. The economically meaningful question is whether the bank earns more than its cost of equity on the tangible capital shareholders have in it. Intrinsic equity = opening tangible book (A$5,306.5m, 30-Jun-26) + PV of residual income (cash earnings less one-offs less CoE x opening TBV) over five years + PV of a Gordon terminal on year-5 residual income. Per-share values divide by 577.15m shares on issue held flat.
valuation_philosophy.wacc_field_note: The 'wacc' field in every scenario is the COST OF EQUITY in AUD, not a blended WACC. Built as AGB 10-year ~4.3% + beta ~1.05 x Australian ERP ~5.5% = ~10.1%, rounded to 10.0% base. Franking credits are ignored in base and bear (conservative for a foreign or tax-exempt holder); bull credits roughly half the ~1.5pp franking benefit via a 9.0% CoE.
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value_note: Terminal value is a Gordon perpetuity on year-5 residual income at 'terminal_growth' (3.0% base). The implied exit P/TBV (terminal equity / Y5 TBV) is reported per scenario and checked against BEN's own FY21-FY26 closing P/NTA range of ~1.05-1.45x; today's 1.14x NTA / 0.90x book sits in the lower third of that range.
valuation_philosophy.timing_note: Periods are fiscal years from the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet (Y1 = FY27), each discounted as a full year from the 21-Sep-2026 valuation date. That over-discounts by ~3 months and omits the residual income earned Jul-Sep 2026; both are conservative and together worth well under A$0.15/share.

inputs.share_count_basis: 577.150m fully paid ordinary shares on issue excluding 2.94m treasury shares at 30-Jun-26 (FY2026 annual report, share capital note line 12373 and NTA table line 4541; matches the filing's NTA/share of $9.19). Held FLAT: SBC (~A$7m/yr equity-settled) is expensed inside cash earnings. The DRP was satisfied on-market (neutralised) for the FY24 and FY25 dividends but by NEW ISSUE for the H1 FY26 interim (10.3m shares, A$142.8m), lifting the count 563.9m -> 577.2m (+2.4%); if that continues, ~13-14m shares/yr are issued at ~1.1x NTA. At ROTE ~= CoE the retained capital earns ~zero residual income, so DRP issuance near intrinsic P/TBV is value-neutral per share and is not modelled as dilution; the cash-dividend assumption is the equivalent. Diluted WANOS of 644.4m includes ~75m shares from convertible loan capital (capital notes) whose distributions are already deducted from profit -- counting them as shares too would double-count. The Metrics.csv figure 566.8 is a mid-year count, not 30-Jun-26.
inputs.net_debt_note: Zero by construction: customer deposits (A$86.0bn) and debt issuance/loan capital (A$10.4bn) are operating funding for a bank, not net debt. The residual-income flow is already after all funding costs, so nothing is subtracted from equity value.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: NOT owner FCF: bank model. This is FY26 cash earnings after tax (A$530.2m), the earnings base the ROTE path is calibrated to (cash ROTE 10.10% on average tangible equity of A$5,247.5m). Owner FCF is undefined for a deposit taker.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report statement of changes in equity, share-based payment A$7.0m (FY26: A$-3.4m reversal on lapsed awards); already expensed inside cash earnings, no separate deduction
inputs.interest_income_note: Not applicable: interest income (A$4,692m FY26) IS the revenue of a bank; nothing is stripped
inputs.buyback_note: No buyback programme. FY25 DRP neutralisation bought A$26.1m of shares on market; FY26 the DRP was satisfied by new issue instead. Base assumes no buybacks through Y5.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-21T06:10:30Z (16:10 AEST, ASX regular close incl. closing auction)
inputs.balance_sheet_source: BEN.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt (NTA table lines 4515-4541; balance sheet line 8824; share capital note lines 12356-12373; cash earnings reconciliation lines 3450-3500; five-year summary lines 8610-8635)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in AUD: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.3% (Sep-2026) + beta ~1.05 x Australian equity risk premium ~5.5% = ~10.1%; 10.0% base, 11.0% bear, 9.0% bull (partial franking credit). A regional bank with a 61.6% cost-to-income ratio and an open AUSTRAC investigation is not lower-risk than the majors, so no discount to the ANZ.AX rate.
inputs.notes: MODEL: residual income on tangible book at cost of equity (dcf-methods routing table, row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'). Owner-FCF DCF rejected because OCF is loan/deposit flow and deposits are not net debt. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry existed. Earnings base: FY25 statutory result is a A$97.1m loss on the A$539.5m Consumer CGU goodwill impairment (non-cash, no TBV effect) and FY26 statutory NPAT of A$375.1m carries A$155.1m of after-tax non-cash items (restructure A$50.6m, APRA rectification provision A$49.0m, Homesafe realised income A$22.7m, penalty A$9.8m, RACQ integration A$6.1m), so the ROTE path is anchored on FY26 cash ROTE (10.10%; H2 10.46%) and one-offs are charged explicitly below cash earnings rather than buried in the ROTE path. FY27 guidance: notable items A$100-123m pre-tax, BAU cost growth 4-5% ex RACQ, RACQ adds A$33-37m NII from 1H27 completion, ROE above 10% by 2030. Price is the ASX regular close; not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (1.2%) and TBV/share CAGR (1.4%) are below the 3.0% used as terminal residual-income growth; 3.0% is the loan/deposit-book growth rate (~3.3-3.9%/yr) net of a little share issuance, which is what drives the capital base of a bank at a constant ROTE. The bank model has no revenue/FCF growth driver.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Statutory EPS CAGRs are negative (3yr -9.2%, 5yr -7.6%) while equity compounded +1.2%/yr: FY26 statutory EPS (65.9c) is depressed by A$155m of after-tax non-cash items (restructure, APRA rectification provision, Homesafe fair value) and FY25 is a loss (-17.2c) on the A$539.5m Consumer CGU goodwill impairment. Cash EPS fell 3.0%/yr over three years (102.1c -> 93.2c) because the FY23 result was a NIM peak (1.94%) with a 54.9% cost-to-income ratio that has since drifted to 61.6%. None of these is a run-rate; the model is driven by ROTE on tangible book.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null by design: operating cash flow of a deposit-taking bank (+A$6.1bn FY21, -A$3.3bn FY22, +A$5.7bn FY23, -A$0.3bn H1 FY26) is loan/deposit flow, not owner earnings. Cash earnings compounded 3.0%/yr FY21-FY26 (457 -> 530) but the FY23 peak (577) means the last three years are -2.8%/yr; TBV/share compounded only 1.4%/yr because ~68% of cash earnings is paid out and the FY25 goodwill write-down (non-cash, no TBV effect) does not explain it -- ROTE of ~10% on a 68% payout retains only ~3.2% of TBV a year, and DRP issuance at ~1.1x NTA adds the rest.

base.terminal_growth_label: perpetual growth of residual income after Y5
base.rationale: Cash ROTE steps 10.3% -> 11.0% from FY26's 10.10% (H2 FY26 annualised 10.46%): FY27 gets RACQ NII (+A$33-37m) and productivity but NIM headwinds and 4-5% BAU cost growth cap it at 10.3%; the lift to 11% by FY30 credits roughly half of the 2030 'ROE above 10%' objective (which needs ~12.5% ROTE). After-tax one-offs of A$80m in FY27 (guided A$100-123m pre-tax notable items), A$50m/A$30m as the ~A$70-90m AML/CTF Financial Crime Transformation Program runs, then A$15m/yr residual. Payout 68% of cash earnings (FY26: 67.6%; target range 60-80%). Cost of equity 10.0%, residual-income growth 3.0% after Y5. With ROTE only ~1pp above CoE, residual income is small and the equity is worth ~1.05x tangible book.

bull.terminal_growth_label: perpetual growth of residual income after Y5
bull.rationale: The 2030 strategy lands: Up's 1.3m customers and the single core platform take cost-to-income from 61.6% toward the mid-50s, NIM holds ~1.95% on the deposit-led funding mix (household deposit-to-loan 76%), and ROTE reaches 12.5% by FY31 (ROE ~10%, the stated objective). Notable items fade after the FY27 A$70m. Payout 65% as retained capital funds RACQ and business/agri growth. Cost of equity 9.0% (half credit for the fully franked dividend, worth ~1.5pp to a domestic holder), growth 3.0%. Implied exit ~1.4x TBV, inside the FY21-FY24 range.

bear.terminal_growth_label: perpetual growth of residual income after Y5
bear.rationale: Mortgage competition and lower cash rates compress NIM back toward 1.80% while BAU costs grow 4-5%: ROTE slips to 9.2% in FY28 and only recovers to 10.0% by FY31 (FY25 was 10.0% and FY22 10.3% on a better rate backdrop). AUSTRAC brings civil penalty proceedings and a ~A$200m penalty lands in FY28, on top of the rectification and AML programs and continuing restructuring (A$120m/A$220m/A$90m/A$50m/A$50m after tax). The board defends the 63c dividend so payout rises to 76%. Cost of equity 11.0%, growth 2.0%. ROTE below CoE makes residual income negative in every year and in perpetuity, so the equity is worth ~0.8x tangible book -- below the ~1.05x NTA BEN bottomed at in 2020 and at the 52-week low (9.81 = 1.07x NTA), because the bear embeds a penalty and a permanent 1pp negative ROTE-CoE spread that the market has never priced.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the scenario's Y1-Y5 dividends and selling at the Y5 intrinsic equity value (TBV + terminal residual income at the scenario CoE) returns 15%/yr. Terminal value is at CoE, not at the hurdle.

required_return_table.note: Base ROTE/payout/one-off path re-discounted at each cost of equity (the equity charge moves with it), terminal growth 3%

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows = cost of equity (%), columns = perpetual growth of residual income after Y5 (%). Base-case ROTE, payout and one-off path.

sensitivity_rote_vs_coe.axis_note: Rows = flat five-year ROTE (%), columns = cost of equity (%). Base one-offs, 68% payout, 3% terminal growth. At ROTE = CoE the value is tangible book less the PV of one-offs (~A$9.0/share).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; bear lifted to 25% and bull cut to 25% because BEN carries fresh APRA licence conditions (18-Aug-26) on non-financial risk, an open AUSTRAC enforcement investigation with an unquantified civil-penalty outcome, a A$50m operational-risk capital overlay, a decade of ROTE at or below the cost of equity (7.4-11.6%), and a 61.6% cost-to-income ratio that is losing share in mortgages. The bull needs the 2030 ROE-above-10% objective to be met on schedule AND a franking-adjusted CoE; the bear needs only FY22-FY25-style ROTE plus a penalty.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide: SBC (~A$7m, 0.35% of income) is expensed inside cash earnings and there is no SBC add-back to dispute, so the house/street band collapses and band_position is null.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.checks_replaced: model is book_value: P/E and EV/EBITDA trip rules do not apply; the historical table is reported for context only
